My analysis in favor of WS2815 (below) remains as a reference, but the decision is made: hands-on experience is more important than theoretical advantage.<x4/><x5/>Practical consequence of WS2811 to keep in mind: pixel = three diodes, so <x6/>cut only at marks<x7/>, and a dead pixel extinguishes everything behind it — hence the spare strip for repair, as we don't solder on the playa.<x8/><x9/><x10/>Reference, why WS2815 is theoretically better:<x11/> <x12/>CLOSED 29.07.2026 — Ivan chose WS2811 and already bought it, testing together.<x13/> Arguments for WS2815 below remain valid as a description of the difference, but the decision is different: we take WS2811, and its main disadvantage (a dead pixel extinguishes everything after it) is mitigated not by a chip, but by <x14/>construction<x15/> — parallel data feed to 8 beams and interchangeable modules on the playa. See "Cutting and changing strip by modules."<x16/><x17/><x18/>The difference is not in brightness, but in three things.<x19/><x20/><x21/><x22/>1. Duplicated signal.<x23/> In WS2811, data goes in a chain: one pixel dies — everything behind it goes dark. On the star beam, this is half an arm in darkness. WS2815 has a second, backup data wire: the signal bypasses the dead pixel, the rest continues to shine.<x24/><x25/><x26/>2. Pixel granularity.<x27/> WS2811 at 12V controls groups of three diodes — one "pixel" is ~10 cm, so our arm 1.20 m = 12 pixels. In WS2815, each diode is controlled: on the same arm, 72 points. For "running water," this is the difference between 10 cm jumps and smooth movement. <x28/>Consequence:<x29/> when switching to WS2815, recalculate animation — there were 96 pixels on the star, it will be ~576 with 60 diodes/m (ESP32 with WLED handles this).<x30/><x31/><x32/>3. Stable current.<x33/> WS2815 maintains brightness when voltage drops along the length. WS2811 noticeably dims by the end of the beam — and our beam is long.<x34/><x35/><x36/>Temperature removed from criteria<x37/> (Ivan, 29.07): during the day, the strip does not work, just stands without current — heats up from the sun, not from itself. <x0/>чому<x1/> · «Біжуча вода» ніколи не: <x0/>why<x1/> · 'Running water' never lights the entire strip at once — only the running front is lit. Previously, the peak was taken as the entire length × W/m at 100% (architect's estimate), and this inflated peak inflated cable and fuse selection. Removed: peak = maximum instantaneous strip fraction × full power (duty_peak). This reduced system peak from 243 to 162 W, and trunk line current to the art — from 20 to 13.5 A. Fraction and W/m are still estimates — test tomorrow will light 1.20 m of 5 m and provide real numbers.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · «Біжуча вода» — це біжу: <x0/>why<x1/> · 'Running water' is a running front, not even lighting of the entire length. At 45% density, strip takes less than half of the nominal 15 W/m. That's why nominal peak Gr.2 of 155 W in real mode turns into 30–75 W: it's not the strip length that decides, but how much of it is lit simultaneously.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · Єдине місце, де просадк: <x0/>Why<x1/> · The only place where voltage drop is really critical is the addressable strip: with a deep drop, both brightness and color will shift along the length. But the peak occurs only in the pathological case of "the whole strip white at full", which does not happen in the "running water" animation. Therefore, instead of pulling even thicker copper for a mode that will never turn on, we set a current limit in WLED — it is made for this. In operating mode, the strip's voltage drop is 3.4% at a 5% limit, at the nominal peak 4.1% — so there is a margin in both modes.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · Головний критерій вибор: <x0/>why<x1/> · Main criterion for lamp selection: when voltage drops, it must REALLY save watts, not maintain the same brightness. In MR16 without driver, current follows voltage, so power drops as square (P ~ V²), and light output — linearly. Practically: at 9 V lamp takes 56% power, giving 75% light — this is the basis of night economy mode. Lamp with stabilizer would not provide such savings.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · Групи треба вміти гасит: <x0/>why<x1/> · Groups need to be extinguished in sequence: when the station runs down, we remove floodlights and decor, but marker lights with stairs remain. If everything hung on one relay, the choice would be only "all or nothing." Common signal from photorelay removed 29.07 — relays themselves remain, the question is only what controls them.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · З трьох ламп, які Іван: <x0/>why<x1/> · Of the three lamps Ivan tested on the power supply through the Greenclick PWM dimmer, Luxrite is the only one that lights evenly at minimum: native Gardencoin shows flicker at low currents. Compatibility with the dimmer was decisive — it can't be found in any specification, only measured on the bench. Currents: 0.52 A at full (6.2 W), 0.02 A and below at minimum, i.e., economy mode range over 26 times. Group of 8 pcs — 4.16 A / 50 W, passes through the dimmer with a 13% margin. Previously Luxrite was rejected as 'phase, not saving from voltage reduction' — this objection related to the plan to throttle voltage and does not apply with PWM dimmer. Voltage run and photo in lm/W not done: Ivan stopped the choice on the winner.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · Кінцевий світильник бач: <x0/>Why<x1/> · The end fixture sees the SUM of voltage drops: trunk line plus branch plus its own lead. Calculating each line separately means underestimating reality by half. <x0/>чому<x1/> · Рішення Івана 31.07. Ка: <x0/>why<x1/> · Ivan's decision 31.07. Cable runs from post to post along the edge, exit to the station directly from the edge — nothing is brought inside the podium. Argument: low power, losses at the last lamp are not critical. Model confirms: on the existing cable, voltage drop to the farthest lamp is within norm, and if the loop is closed and power is brought to one point — it drops even more. Scheme with a central box (hub-method of garden light manufacturers) rejected: it provides more even brightness but pulls extra copper inside and 8 pairs in one box.
<x0/>чому<x1/> · Стрічку ріжемо на 9 від: <x0/>Why<x1/> · Cut the strip into 9 segments (circle + 8 rays), i.e., <x2/>18 ends<x3/>, plus three taps for power — about 24 points total. Half the ends with wire (cap with hole), half blind. Take with ×1.5 reserve, as no rework on the playa.<x4/><x5/><x6/>Two mistakes that kill the work:<x7/><x8/>1. <x9/>Acetic silicone.<x10/> Regular construction sealant releases acetic acid when curing (smells like vinegar) — it corrodes copper traces and contacts. The strip will work, then start dimming in sections after months, and the cause will be elusive. Need <x11/>neutral<x12/> (neutral cure), preferably electronics-grade.<x13/>2. <x14/>Hot glue.<x15/> Gun glue holds up to about 60-70°C, and on the playa, it's 45 in the shade and much more in the sun and black silicone. It will flow during operation — the cap will slide, dust and moisture will get inside.<x16/><x17/><x18/>Steps for each cut:<x19/> cut strictly on the mark (in WS2811 pixel — three diodes, cutting off-mark kills the whole group) → clean and tin contacts → solder wire → fill cap with neutral silicone and fit so silicone protrudes and seals the cut completely → let fully cure (neutral dries longer than acetic, up to a day) → only then test in operation.<x20/><x21/><x22/>What to glue with and why not with a gun.<x23/> Need a small tube at hand, not a cartridge for a gun: about 24 cuts, each a drop, and an open 300 ml tube will dry between sessions. Suitable <x24/>ASI 388 Electronic Grade<x25/> 2.8 oz (~$10) or GE Advanced Silicone 2.8 oz (~$8) — both neutral. Do not take regular clear RTV from auto store: it's usually acetic.<x26/><x27/><x28/>And separately about the glue gun that heats.<x29/> It's not just that regular hot glue flows from heat. The main thing is: <x30/>almost nothing sticks to silicone<x31/> — neither hot glue, nor epoxy, nor superglue. Silicone tube has such a surface that glue just peels off as a film. Only silicone sticks to silicone. Therefore, even high-temperature hot glue (polyamide, holds 120°C) is not an option here — it will withstand the heat but will peel off the tube.<x32/><x33/><x34/>Check caps against the cross-section of your strip<x35/> — they are not universal: there are 6×12, 12×12, 16×16 mm, etc. Buy after measuring the one that has already arrived.
